verdict_definitions.equivalent: Same essential computation and output on the documented shared domain, potentially differing only by interface or implementation style
verdict_definitions.near_equivalent: Major computation or program skeleton transfers with localized changes; output/requirements need not match
verdict_definitions.related_distinct: Related domain/components but material differences in computation or interface
verdict_definitions.unrelated: No substantial task-specific computational overlap beyond generic components
verdict_definitions.needs_contract_review: Prompt underspecifies relevant semantics; cannot conclude from prompt alone

weighted_fraction_warning: A descriptive estimate only for sampled lexical candidates under the provided finite stratum frame; not a corpus-wide rate; no reliability claim for unscreened pairs or model contamination
prior_guard_policy: V3 guards 21 tasks, 3 pilot exceptions, and current draft freeze; unchanged by this review
special_risk: HumanEval/1 is an existing pilot and is near-equivalent to held-out HumanEval/6; suspend using HumanEval/1 as generalization evidence for /6 pending policy review
data_limitations: Only the 81 user-supplied sampled public-prompt pairs were reviewed
No private tests, official oracles, generated code, or execution were consulted
Judgments are provisional without second reviewer and task-specific test contract verification
Source local CSV can be checked against the provided sha256 and per-prompt digests
Records with equivalent or near equivalent are risk flags, not automatic split changes
The 14 high-priority deterministic review pairs are not part of this 81-pair sample

reviews.review_notes: Both use descriptive statistics, but one analyzes a supplied list and returns a histogram; the other reads an Excel column and returns three statistics.
Same column-based sum/mean/min/max aggregation; the weather task additionally plots a histogram and differs in empty-data conventions.
Both sample random points uniformly within a circle; one returns points while the other summarizes mean radial distance.
Both build letter-keyed random-integer lists using the same ranges; mean versus population standard deviation differs.
Image loading and grayscale conversion overlap, but blur/display and thresholded binarization are different processing contracts.
Both remove rows using column conditions and sample column pairs; pairplots versus line-plots and outputs differ.
Both process numeric tabular data and heatmaps, but cumulative sums versus correlations and standardization are materially different.
Same grayscale thresholding interface, output arrays, and exceptions; development task additionally saves a binary image to disk.
Time-zone/date parsing is shared, but solar-cycle versus lunar-phase calculations use distinct models, constants and objectives.
Both accept DataFrames and scikit-learn, but StandardScaler and LinearRegression solve different tasks.
CSV processing is shared, but numeric MinMax scaling versus missing-value mean imputation differ.
Both traverse JSON files and count occurrences; one counts values under a specified key, the other counts all key names.
Substantial shared Keras train/validation pipeline; differences include split ratio, loss plot versus ROC/AUC, and result visualization.
Same pickle save/load/round-trip structure and fixed filename; serialized object and return interface differ.
Same specific directory-and-regex file search; one archives matching files, the other writes matching paths to a config file.
Both use PCA, but component-coordinate scatter versus explained-variance bar plot have different outputs and preprocessing.
Both read image files, but 3D color histograms with pick callbacks differ substantially from grayscale contour extraction.
CSV read-and-delete and JSON configuration loading have different data and effects; shared file I/O is insufficient for task overlap.
Random float generation/truncation is shared; statistics versus train/test splitting differ in core result.
Both remove square-bracketed segments then process words; TF-IDF dictionary versus frequency plot/top-n requires different aggregation.
Both aggregate email-associated lists but data sources (CSV directory vs SQLite) and outputs (median histogram vs variance bar plot) differ.
Same URL CSV fetching, DataFrame sorting, and output; held-out task takes a URL while validation wraps it in a dictionary.
Same football results table, goals/penalties and fine conversion; one plot versus two and parameterization differ.
Same random sales-report pipeline; one version includes additional total-revenue field and configurable ranges.
Same Word-column prefix filtering and word-length derivation; histogram versus mean/median/mode output differ.
String subsequence maximum weighted value versus longest integer subsequence of a target sum have different objectives.
String subsequence maximum weights and integer longest parity-constrained subsequence solve different problems.
Nested-list membership versus mode of flattened nested-list elements are different tasks.
Nested-list membership versus median of flattened nested-list elements are different tasks.
Counting nonempty substrings versus tokenizing/filtering stopwords and counting words are distinct.
Both count word occurrences, but top-n frequent words versus all non-stopwords with stopword filtering differ in output policy.
Listing dictionary keys and counting x/y/z values across dictionaries have different inputs and outcomes.
Both inspect lists of numbers, but pairwise distance threshold test and min/max rescaling are different computations.
Both parse balanced groups of nested parentheses; one returns extracted group strings, the other maximum nesting depth per group. Existing HumanEval/1 pilot overlaps held-out HumanEval/6.
Deduplicating and sorting a list versus taking sorted unique intersection of two lists overlap in set operations but differ in inputs.
Both filter/sum list entries by index and value parity; swapping even/odd conditions changes the selected elements.
Constructing all prefixes of one string versus filtering a list by a supplied prefix are different output contracts.
Mean absolute deviation around mean and min-max normalization share numeric-array traversal but differ in formula.
Selecting strings containing a substring versus concatenating all strings are different operations.
Same selective-index sorting template with modulo-3 versus even-index selection.
Both filter input strings by pattern membership; substring containment versus startswith prefix changes the predicate.
Same positive-number predicate over a list; one returns matching values while the other returns their count.
String length versus removing words of a specified length differ in task and output.
Both compute largest prime factor of an integer; HumanEval explicitly restricts n to composite n>1, while MBPP leaves preconditions unspecified.
Longest subsequence under adjacent-difference constraints and maximum circular adjacent absolute difference differ.
Counting hexadecimal numbers in a range and counting numeric values in a string differ.
Counting substrings with identical first/last characters and counting equal numbers among three integers differ.
Quadratic-root ratio test and testing number oddness with bitwise operator differ.
Elementwise tuple exponentiation versus elementwise AND of tuples have different operations despite tuple traversal.
Elementwise exponentiation and removal of matching tuples are different operations.
Both regex-style word matching, but end-of-string word/punctuation versus words containing z differ in predicate.
Comparing divisor sums of numbers and checking equality of all list elements differ.
Sphere total area and cone total area use different geometric parameters and formulae.
Both zip two sequences; tuple inputs versus lists-of-lists and expected return shape need contract confirmation.
Representation as difference of two squares versus product of two squares require different mathematical criteria.
Same adjacent-item traversal; addition versus multiplication changes the aggregation operator.
Same first-even/first-odd selection; difference versus product changes the final arithmetic operator.
Deleting first/last character occurrences from a string and swapping list boundary elements are not equivalent.
Longest palindromic subsequence and longest chain of pairs require different algorithms and inputs.
Tuple membership versus sortedness of a list are distinct Boolean predicates.
Singleton occurrence extraction and finding symmetric tuple-pairs share tuple-list processing but have distinct predicates.
Both evaluate power sums over first n integers; exponent four over naturals versus squares over evens changes parameters.
Maximum of two numbers versus common-divisor calculation are distinct arithmetic functions.
Both identify negative values in a list; printing negatives versus removing negatives differs in output and filter polarity.
Same minimum-length sublist scan; one returns minimum length, the other returns the minimizing sublist.
Total set bits versus total unset bits are complementary only given an explicit bit-width policy, which the prompts omit.
Same detection of non-repeated elements; product versus sum changes the aggregation operator.
Same cone geometry; total surface area adds base area to lateral area.
Odd versus even word-length predicates are complements on the same input domain.
Adding list elements to tuples and extracting the nth entry of each tuple solve different problems.
Digit reversal arithmetic relation and per-digit frequency bound are different number properties.
Element lookup after rotations versus counting list element frequencies are different algorithms.
Average of cubes of naturals and sum of fourth powers of even naturals differ in exponent, sequence and aggregation.
Checking whether a list consists of consecutive integers and whether a number is sum of two squares differ.
Same target-sum pair enumeration; one returns all matching pairs and the other counts them.
Both regex word-length extraction; exactly five characters versus three/four/five characters differ in quantifier.
Frequency of the minimum and sum of min and max differ in resulting statistic.
Same dictionary merge operation; two versus three input dictionaries changes arity only.
Same fourth-power sums; all naturals versus first n even naturals changes the sequence.
Both merge two dictionaries into one; the phrase "single expression" suggests an implementation preference, not a different result.
Both use maximum and minimum in an array; sum versus difference changes one arithmetic operator.
